holidays.name: National Hot Chocolate Day
holidays.description: A cozy day to wrap your hands around a steaming mug of cocoa, ideally topped with a mountain of marshmallows or whipped cream, as an excuse to ward off the last bitter chill of January.
holidays.origin: Like many American food observances, it grew out of informal food-lover and marketing traditions rather than an official proclamation. Its placement in late January targets the heart of cold-weather season.
holidays.funFact: The Aztecs drank a bitter, spicy chocolate beverage long before sugar was added. Europeans later sweetened it with sugar and milk, creating the hot chocolate we know today.

holidays.name: National Brandy Alexander Day
holidays.description: A salute to the creamy, dessert-like cocktail made with brandy, crème de cacao, and cream, usually finished with a dusting of nutmeg. It is a sweet send-off to the first month of the year.
holidays.origin: The cocktail dates to the early 20th century and was popular in the 1920s and beyond. The unofficial day is a cocktail-lover observance created to celebrate its rich flavor.
holidays.funFact: The Brandy Alexander is said to have been a favorite of John Lennon, who reportedly drank many during his famous 'Lost Weekend' period in the 1970s.

holidays.name: Inspire Your Heart with Art Day
holidays.description: A day for letting a painting, sculpture, song, or doodle touch your soul. You are encouraged to visit a gallery, create something, or simply admire art that moves you.
holidays.origin: The observance was founded by artist and author Katherine Lee-Gabbert to encourage people to connect emotionally with art, and it is celebrated each year on January 31.
holidays.funFact: Studies have suggested that looking at art can trigger pleasure responses in the brain similar to those produced by seeing someone you love.

holidays.name: Backward Day
holidays.description: A topsy-turvy day when people wear their clothes backward, eat dessert before dinner, say goodbye instead of hello, and walk in reverse, all in the name of silliness.
holidays.origin: Backward Day is an informal, humor-driven observance with no single documented founder. It spread through novelty-holiday calendars and school activities, since it is easy for classrooms and offices to join in.
holidays.funFact: Many people celebrate by eating breakfast for dinner, which is likely the easiest and tastiest way to take part in the day.

holidays.name: Gorilla Suit Day
holidays.description: A gloriously ridiculous holiday on which people are encouraged to put on a gorilla suit and go about their business as if nothing is unusual, from grocery shopping to office meetings.
holidays.origin: Gorilla Suit Day is an unofficial novelty observance that appears in lists of offbeat holidays. Its origins are murky, but it has endured thanks to the timeless comedic appeal of a person in an ape costume.
holidays.funFact: Early gorilla suits were popular in classic Hollywood films, and in many cases the actors inside them were human performers rather than real apes, which made 'a man in a gorilla suit' a long-running movie trope.
